persona.title: PhD Candidate — Aerospace Engineering
bio: Aerospace engineer finishing a PhD at Politecnico di Torino, where my work sits at the intersection of human factors, knowledge engineering, and flight simulation.

I am drawn to complexity — the steeper the learning curve, the more engaged I become. Throughout my academic path I have shifted research focus more than once, each time diving deep into unfamiliar territory, and I see that adaptability as one of my strongest assets.
I tend to be analytical and patient, both at work and outside it. I value the effort behind results as much as the results themselves, and I bring that same care to every commitment I take on.
I am now looking for roles — in R&D or research — where curiosity is a job requirement and no two problems look the same.

NLP (BERT fine-tuning, text classification), speech recognition (Whisper), ontology design (OWL/RDF, Protégé), knowledge graphs (Neo4j, Cypher).
A320 FNPT II full-flight simulator, Tobii eye-tracking systems, multi-modal data acquisition and fusion, experimental test design.
Linux, Docker, MS Office, technical writing, scientific presenting.
